maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL

speechtext:
The house resumed from Friday, April 7, consideration in committee of Bill No. 37, respecting the Canadian National Railways and to provide for cooperation with the Canadian Pacific Railway system and for other purposes.-Mr. Manion.-Mr. Sullivan in the chair.
On section 2.-His Majesty bound.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
When the bill was last under consideration there was before the committee an amendment moved by the hon. member for West Lamb ton (Mr. Gray) that there should be added to section 2 another subsection, (d). Certain questions were raised in the discussion and some observations were made both by the Minister of Railways and by the Prime Minister. The minister contended on that occasion

CM.R.-C.P.R. Bill
that under this bill the trustees to be appointed were to be subject to the Board of Railway Commissioners. He held that there were in this bill the same powers as contained in the Canadian National Railways Act of 1920, while we on this side maintained that this was not so. In the legislation of 1920, with respect to the abandonment of branch lines, the Canadian National Railways were subject in the first instance to the Board of Railway Commissioners and they were also subject to the approval of the Governor General in Council, and we pointed out that under this bill these two safeguards were being removed. We contended that the trustees were no longer subject to the Governor General in Council or to this parliament, if this bill went through in its present form, and the minister endeavoured to prove the opposite. Has he anything to add this afternoon with regard to the construction of the legislation?

speakeroldname: Hon. R. J. MANION (Minister of Railways) :
maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
Naturally I have made further inquiries and they have merely strengthened the position I took when the bill was under consideration before. After a thorough study of the question and consultation with the legal branch of the department as well as with an outstanding legal gentleman not connected with the department, I am strengthened in the opinion I expressed on that occasion, namely, that so far at least as part I is concerned the trustees are in exactly the same position as the directors, and the insertion of this amendment would therefore make no difference with respect to part I. Under section 9, subsection 2, the trustees are given the same powers and are restricted in the same manner as the directors. I will read the provision again, although I put it on Hansard on the former occasion:
The trustees shall and may thereafter, subject to the provisions of this act. have and exercise all the powers, rights, privileges and immunities, and perform and be subject to all the duties, responsibilities and restrictions, which now appertain to the board of directors of the national company.
In reply to that, my hon. friend from Vancouver Centre and some other hon. members opposite pointed out that subsection 6 of section 9 conflicted with subsection 2 which I have just read. Subsection 6 reads:
No order, regulation, by-law, act, decision or proceeding of the trustees shall require the approval of His Majesty or that of any other shareholder of any company to which this section applies.
This applies only in so far as the governor in council acts as shareholder of the company. As pointed out by the Prime Minister, the governor in council has a dual capacity. On
some occasions it acts as shareholder and on others as representative of the parliament of Canada; it is the executive of parliament and acts in that capacity, as will be seen by reference to section 151 of the Railway Act.
I adhere therefore to the opinion that the incorporation of section 23 of the Canadian National Railway Act into this part of the bill now under consideration would have no effect on the trustees so far as part I is concerned, whereas it might interfere with the actions of the trustees in cooperating with the Canadian Pacific Railway. So that it would be unnecessary for part I to include that section, while it would perhaps be harmful so far as parts II and III are concerned.
The Canadian Pacific Railway can to-day abandon lines without appearing before the Board of Railway Commissioners at all, but the Canadian National Railways are not in the same position; they cannot abandon branch lines without appearing before the board, even under this section. I maintain therefore that this amendment is unnecessary and indeed might be harmful.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: Does the minister contend now that the board of trustees must have the authority of the governor in council before there can be abandonment of branch lines?

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: Of the Board of Railway Commissioners. Yes, so far as the Canadian National Railways are concerned, even under this bill. That is my contention.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: Under this bill, then, the Canadian Pacific Railway will no longer be able to abandon lines.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
Under this bill the Canadian Pacific Railway will be in exactly the same position as it was before. To-day it can abandon lines without reference to the Board of Railway Commissioners at all, but the Canadian National cannot. In other words, the Canadian National has been throughout, from that point of view, at an advantage or a disadvantage, just as you wish to take it.	At any rate, the Canadian
National could not abandon a line without submission to the Board of Railway Commissioners of Canada whereas the Canadian Pacific could and will still be able to.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
In making an application for a branch line, has the Canadian Pacific to meet the same conditions in getting a charter as the Canadian National? That is, must the charter be subject to the approval of the railway commission?
C.N.R.-C.P.R. Bill

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: The charter is not obtained from the board, it is granted by this house. The Canadian Pacific and the Canadian National both have to come before a committee of this house in order to obtain a charter, and both companies will be in the same position in the future as they have been in the past. It will be perhaps a little more difficult for them to obtain charters as I think the committee will agree that charters have been granted a little too freely in the past.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
Do I understand the
minister aright? I understand him to say that all charters are granted by this house and that the railway commission would have the right to nullify such charters. The commission may grant to the Canadian National the right to discontinue a branch line but the Canadian Pacific may take this action without appearing before the commission.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
That has been the law
throughout.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: May I ask the minister just what action has been necessary by the Canadian National in the past in regard to the abandoning of branch lines?

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
There is no doubt that
branch lines have been abandoned but I could not name .any particular instance at the moment.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: There was a line at Jasper.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: Not to any great degree? Mr. MANION:	That is quite right.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: Supposing a proposal was made by one company to the other in regard to the abandonment of a line. If they could not agree a tribunal would be set up. Would it be possible for that tribunal to give a decision as to the abandonment of a line without the company appearing before the Board of Railway Commissioners and the governor in council?

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: One of the clauses of the bill provides that if a tribunal is set up in connection with a matter which, but for the provisions of this act, would require the approval of the Board of Railway Commissioners, no order of a tribunal shall be operative without the assent and concurrence of the chairman, who is also the chairman of the Board of Railway Commissioners.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: But not the board?

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
No, not the board. He
is the chairman of the Board of Railway Commissioners, and in a sense the two bodies are in a similar position. I should like to

elaborate upon a point to which I referred a moment ago. Under this legislation it is provided that if one company should decide to build a branch line and the other company took the attitude that such a line was not necessary, that its construction would be extravagant or wasteful due to the fact that the same service could be given by common running rights, this would be considered a proper matter for determination by a tribunal. The tribunal might come to the decision that the construction of the particular branch line would be extravagant and unnecessary as the same service could be given through common running rights.
Mr. VALLAN'CE:	Will it still be necessary for either company to come to this house when applying for charters?

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
Yes, just the same as in
the past.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: Then the tribunal could go contrary to this house which has granted the charter?

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: Yes, it could.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
The tribunal is to be
supreme over parliament?

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
It is all a matter of
economy. Might I suggest that it would have been better in the past if some such tribunal had been set up to restrain the useless duplication and extravagance which has taken place. I do not think anyone will deny that if such a tribunal had been set up there would have been no duplication of hotel facilities at Halifax or at Vancouver. The same thing would apply to the building of many branch lines as I have no doubt that in a number of instances the same territories could have been served by common running rights or joint operation.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
I was rather alarmed at
the statement made a few moments ago by the minister to the effect that the Canadian Pacific could abandon lines without the permission of the Board of Railway Commissioners. The railway employees have always been dependent upon section 179 of the Railway Act.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
That section covers
terminals and divisional points.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
If you abandon any section of a line, surely you abandon a terminal. Section 179 reads:
The company shall not, at any time, make any change, alteration or deviation in the railway, or any portion thereof, until the provisions of the last preceding section are fully complied with,-

C.N.R.-C.P.R. Bill
That is to say, the municipalities and others are to have the right to appear before the Board of Railway Commissioners. The section continues:
*-nor remove, close, or abandon any station, or divisional point nor create a new divisional point which would involve the removal of employees, without leave of the board;
I think the minister should develop this point a little further as I am rather alarmed at his statement.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
As the minister knows, I am not a lawyer but I have a book here which I am able to read, as I learned to do that at one time. Section 179 reads:
The company shall not, at any time, make any change, alteration or deviation in the railway, or any portion thereof, until the provisions of the last preceding section are fully complied with.
The preceding section provides that the railway cannot make any deviation, change or alteration without submission to the board. It is alarming to me to find out that the Canadian Pacific Railway is not subject to this law the same as the Canadian National Railways.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: What is it my hon. friend is worrying about? Is it the abandonment of lines that is bothering him?

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
I am alarmed about the
whole bill.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
I have no doubt the hon.
gentleman is.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
The minister has just
made a statement that is new and alarming to me because he said that the Canadian Pacific could abandon branch lines-I think he used the words "branch lines"-

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: Any line.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: -without first appearing before the Board of Railway Commissioners and getting leave, but that the Canadian National Railway could not do so; consequently our railway employees who secured the insertion of section 179 have been labouring under a misapprehension all these years.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: And it is to remain in force.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
What is the use of its
remaining in force if the company does not live up to it?

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
To come back to my former
point, do I understand the minister correctly that in all matters in which the railway companies will have powers under this legislation, when any dispute arises, the arbitral tribunal which is to be set up, will have power under the Railway Act and over that of the Board of Railway Commissioners?

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
The question of arbitral
tribunals does not arise until we reach part III of the measure, and in a discussion of one clause I do not like to deal with the whole bill because it is a little difficult to deal with it in that way. Let me point out to my hon. friend that when a tribunal is set up, the chairman of the Board of Railway Commissioners is automatically chairman of that tribunal and as regards any matter which would ordinarily be referred to the railway board, he must assent in writing or no order of a tribunal will be operative. So that at any rate the chairman of the Board of Railway Commissioners, being also chairman of the arbitral tribunal, is in a position similar to that of chairman of the railway board if there is possibility of some public interest being interfered with. I do not know whether I have made myself clear, but I have tried to do so.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
With this difference: a matter may go before the Board of Railway Commissioners and it is possible for that board to give one decision and the chairman to give another when a matter comes before the tribunal.
C.N.R.-C.P.R. Bill

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
If the arbitral tribunal
makes one decision and the Board of Railway Commissioners makes another, the decision of the arbitral tribunal prevails.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: Has the minister not got this the wrong way round? He makes the chairman of the arbitral tribunal decide first, and then the Board of Railway Commissioners, which is there to watch the larger public interest, gives a second decision. Should the Board of Railway Commissioners as a whole not be regarded as more important than its chairman?

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
I do not think my right
hon. friend has seen the point I made. In a case where the arbitral tribunal have decided on a matter which ordinarily would go before the Board of Railway Commissioners, the chairman of the tribunal has to put in writing his agreement with the decision of the arbitral tribunal if the decision is to prevail and then the matter does not go before the railway board at all. But he, being by virtue of his position, also chairman of the railway board, is in a position to judge as to the public interest involved. There is no reason why he should give two decisions; he gives one.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
Why should
the matter not go before the Board of Railway Commissioners ait the outsat without troubling about the arbitral tribunal? If the Board of Railway Commissioners are going to decide the public interest part of the matter, should they not have the first say?

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
These are matters that
do not in the very nature of things come within the ordinary statutory jurisdiction of the Board of Railway Commissioners, otherwise it would not be necessary to set up the arbitral tribunal which, of course, has no reference to the matter under consideration. An arbitral tribunal might not be set up during the whole ten years or more, let us say, of the operations of this measure. An arbitral tribunal comes into being only when there is a direct and specific matter to be considered which remains unsettled after negotiation between the heads of the railways. If they fail to agree, this tribunal comes into being, but not otherwise. There can be no setting up of an arbitral tribunal unless they have failed to agree.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
But that
raises the larger question why the Board of Railway Commissioners might not act as an arbitral tribunal instead of making all these special provisions for such a tribunal where in the end 'there will have to be an appeal to the railway board.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
With deference to the
rtgiht hon. gentleman, not appeal to the Board of Railway Commissioners. The principle of the finding of the transportation commission is-and i't seems to me iit is sound-having regard to the extraordinary powers vested in the trustees and to the possibility of arranging matters so as to effect economy, and having regard to the possibility of difference of opinion between the heads of the two systems with respect not to matters over which the Board of Railway Commissioners has jurisdiction but to a matter within the purview of 'the present statute, there is to be set up this tribunal; because iit was regarded as fairer to both the interested corporations, the Canadian National system and the Canadian Pacific system, that this specific dispute shall be settled, but that advantage should be taken of the knowledge and experience of the chairman of the Board of Railway Commissioners by his being made a member of the arbitral tribunal. That is, I understand, the theory on which the legislation was based.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: But does this not all come down pretty much to a matter of designation? The chairman of the Board of Railway Commissioners is the important factor. In one case he is called president or chairman of the arbitral tribunal and in the other he is chairman of the Board of Railway Commissioners. Why have the arbitral tribunal at all if this one person is really to be the deciding factor? Why not say in this bill at once as in others: We will enlarge the scope of the jurisdiction of the Board of Railway Commissioners and it will deal with these matters, thus cutting out the part concerned with the arbitral tribunals.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
The answer to that is
that the Duff commission in its wisdom made a recommendation to the contrary. It believed this course to be wiser, and the Senate committee, which was composed of representatives of both parties, was practically unanimously in favour of it. Even in the final decision there were only two or three who expressed any dissent from the almost complete unanimity in regard to this method of dealing with disputes.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
We are not the Duff commission; we are the House of Commons, a part of parliament. The fact that the Duff commission makes a recommendation of which the minister cannot show the virtue, does not help the situation in any way. The minister has not made out any case for these arbitral tribunals.

C.N.R.-C.P.R. Bill

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: Mention some of them.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: I think I could mention at least $100,000,000 worth.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: What are they?

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: Take as examples the Halifax hotel, the Vancouver hotel. They make rtp about $15,000,000 between them. Then there are the Montreal terminals, $50,000,000 and the acquisition of obsolete and well nigh useless lines, that had never paid their way and may never do so.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: Does the minister think this bill will prevent such occurrences in the future?

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: Yes, an arbitral tribunal could prevent proposed extravagances and duplications, perhaps not the buying of lines. They certainly could have prevented the building of hotels, the Montreal terminals and the spending of $8,000,000 on those triangle tour steamships on the Pacific. Those four items alone amount to about $73,000,000. They certainly could have prevented tens of millions of dollars being spent on branch lines, many of which were a duplication of other branch lines already in existence. Speaking just from memory there are about eighty or ninety millions of dollars which they could have prevented from being spent. I am not saying that with a view to criticizing anybody, but rather to indicate that the arbitral tribunal provision is justified because the leader of the opposition suggests that a case has not been made out to justify such an arrangement.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: My objection was not to having some body to which reference could be made for these purposes, but was to having an arbitral tribunal of which the chairman of the railway commission was to be the chairman, as distinct from the railway commission itself doing this work at the outset. While I do not admit for a moment that what the minister has said is correct, nevertheless if that were so, the argument would be equally strong if the railways had to go in the first instance before a commission already established rather than before some body constituted following this legislation.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: May I say something to justify the establishment of an arbitral tribunal as a principle. Taking my hon. friend's own argument, the chairman of the arbitral tribunal has had, as chairman of the railway commission, a couple of years of actual experience which in my judgment should make him eminently satisfactory as a judge of general railway matters. He has that advantage. Secondly, the arbitral tribunal has this superiority over the railway commission, that it is presided over by the chairman of the railway commission and there are also on the tribunal a representative of each of the railway companies concerned. You have those three men on the tribunal and they will not sit as does the Board of Railway Commissioners merely as a judicial body,. because of course the members of the railway commission are judges just as those presiding over the appeal court and the exchequer court, and they cannot be expected to go into the details of things as an arbitral tribunal could do. The chairman of the Board of Railway Commissioners, sitting as chairman of a tribunal, with the representatives of the two railway companies may sit down and have a round table conference over any railway matter at issue. I might say quite frankly that I have had the opinion expressed to me by the highest officials of both railway companies that that would be the greatest advantage of a tribunal, that they could meet at a round table conference rather than with the formality, or the fuss and feathers as one hon. member suggests, of a court. I believe myself in all sincerity that the arbitral tribunal as proposed is a type of tribunal superior to the Board of Railway Commissioners for that purpose. That is my own personal view, but after all it is a matter of opinion.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
What about the tariff board? Why should not they do the same, have a round table conference?
C.N.R.-C.P.R. Bill

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: I do not want to get off on to the tariff board at the present time because we have troubles enough with .this bill.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: The chairman of the tribunal, who is also the chairman of the railway commission, is assisted by a representative of each of the railway companies on the tribunal, and the tribunal can come to no decision unless the chairman assents to it. He must be satisfied. Is not that right? So why not just enlarge the powers of the railway commission, because in the final analysis the chairman of the railway commission must be satisfied.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: I take it that the committee is desirous of expediting this bill which we are] aow discussing. With respect to Part III, I would have a few observations that I think might be of some value to the committee when that stage is reached. I had thought that this was merely an incidental discussion, but I do think that if we are going to make any progress with the bill we should confine ourselves to the section before us. When Part III comes up to be considered it is not impossible that the house might .make out a case that Part III should not be there at all. That is a matter that will have to be considered by the committee as a whole when the moment arises, but I do suggest that if we desire to make any progress we should deal with the sections as they come before us.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
Would the
Prime Minister be agreeable to the committee reverting to different sections and reopening the discussion on them if, in the light of further discussion of other parts of the bill, that is found advisable, because what we are discussing now is very vital in view of our interpretation of the bill? But of course the government may put another interpretation upon it.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
I have always thought
that it was a very proper course to pursue if, in the light of discussions taking place in committee, it is thought desirable to reconsider a particular section, that the house should at the conclusion of its discussion revert to it. As far as I am concerned, I have always followed that course, and I think it is a sound one. It would merely mean that in the light of further knowledge and greater wisdom we desired to reconsider a certain section. Certainly I think that should be so, and especially with a bill of this character.

But I do feel that the ordinary rules of procedure should be adhered to, and that we should not discuss Part III when we are dealing with a section such as this.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
The reason
possibly that more time is being taken in committee at the moment than might otherwise have been the case is that this bill did not go to the committee on railways and canals or to a special committee as it should have done. Might I say to the Prime Minister that some suggestion has been made that other bills which have been before committees of another house might not go to committees of this house? I think that we in this house ought to maintain strictly the privileges of our own house and that when-we wish to be enlightened with respect to a particular measure it should go before a committee of the House of Commons. This bill should certainly have gone before a select standing or special committee of this house, and then we would have come here in a position to run through the sections understanding their whole significance. But inasmuch as the Prime Minister himself stated that this bill would have to be considered m committee of the whole in this house, I think additional latitude must be expected in the matter of discussion.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: I am not going to waste the time of the committee beyond saying this, that not in my time has any bill been as adequately considered as this particular bill was by a committee of the Senate.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
We are not the
Senate.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: Some of you would like to be. Might I observe that the Right Hon. George Graham, who was at one time Minister of Railways, presided over that Senate committee?

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: He is not responsible to any constituency to-day.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
Just permit me to conclude what I have to say, and that is this, that the evidence taken before that committee was made available to the members of this house. Very few of the members of this house who are now discussing this bill would give anything like the attention and attendance upon a committee that they could give to reading the evidence that was given before the Senate committee. When my right hon. friend says that if the bill had been considered by a committee of this house we could then run through the sections here, that does

C.N.R.-C.P.R. Bill
not mean that the right hon. gentleman himself is going to attend the House of Commons committee. As a matter of fact, he cannot do it and discharge the duties of his office, and therefore he will be dependent for his information upon what he reads and what is said to him. Nor would the ex-Minister of Justice nor other members of the house be in any different position. There was no desire in any way to curtail or lessen inquiry with respect to this legislation. It was introduced into the Senate because it was believed that a more adequate opportunity would be offered there for dispassionate and free discussion and criticism of its provisions than could possibly happen if the bill was dealt with originally in this house and sent to a committee of the House of Commons, to be wrangled over and then sent back to the house, where the whole *discussion would be gone over again. I venture to say this, and I know the committee will not misunderstand me, that Lord Ashfield told me in December in England that he could not recall any committee that he had known in his time that had given finer thought and consideration to a measure affecting transportation than had the Senate committee to this bill as he read their reports.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
He has
not seen us in action.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: He has seen striking evidence of the house being in inaction, and I am not sure that if he were here this afternoon he might not think that was the case today. If I were asked to say what progress we are making with respect to section 2, after an elaborate legal argument the other evening based on an entire misapprehension of section 6, subsection 4

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: There is a difference of opinion about that.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
It is open to argument
always, and that is the reason we have courts. But I do suggest that if we desire to expedite the passage of the bill or to see that intelligent discussion takes place with respect to it it is not good to jump to part III when we are considering section 2.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
I have no desire as a member of this committee to stop the pro-greiss of the bill. As to the wrangling that is going on in the house now, I will remind the Prime Minister that we amended the Canada Grain Act some two or three years ago, and wrangled for two weeks in a committee of the house specially set up, and when the bill came
into the house it took only a few hours to go through. I feel that if this bill had had the same treatment probably it would have been through by now.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: If it had been introduced in the Commons it would.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: As I understand it, the immediate point is whether or not we are preserving the supervisory power of the governor in council and the Board of Railway Commissioners with regard to the abandonment of lines. I understand that it is urged upon the Minister of Railways-if he will permit me to put it that way-by these eminent legal gentlemen, that subsection 6 of section 9 is not inconsistent with section 23 of the Canadian National Railways Act, because subsection 6 of section 9 has to do with His Majesty in his capacity as shareholder, and still leaves the powers of the governor in council as set out in section 23. But what about the power of the Board of Railway Commissioners under section 23; is that still extant? Is my hon. friend satisfied on that point?

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: Yes, as far as part I of this bill is concerned my best legal information is that the Board of Railway Commissioners and the board of trustees stand in exactly the same position under this bill as the directors stood to that board in the past. The arbitral tribunals may make a difference, but as far as concerns part I which deals distinctly with the Canadian National, my best information is that the position will continue exactly the same under this bill as it has been in the past.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: Will my right hon. friend amplify that, so that we may have the facts? Subsection 6 of section 9 provides that no order, regulation, by-law, etc., of the trustees shall require the consent of His Majesty qua shareholder?

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: That is right.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: Are there in fact any shareholders? I know there is provision in the Canadian National Railways Act for shareholders, but have shares ever been issued?

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: Yes, I understand there are shares of the Grand Trunk and the Canadian Northern-

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: But shares of the Canadian National Railway Company?

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
Yes, the Minister of Finance holds shares.
C.N.R.-C.P.R. Bill

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: How many shares, and how long have they been held?

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: I do not know.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: Since the start, I believe, after the order in council was passed following itihe decision of the privy council in the Grand Trunk arbitration. I do not think the hon. member was a member of the government at that time. An order in council was passed by which the shareholders as existing on the register of the Grand Trunk were eliminated, and the Minister of Finance was substituted as a shareholder. With respect to the Canadian National the Shares are held by His Majesty, and there is in one section of the act provision that His Majesty shall he the shareholder. I took tihe trouble to look it up not long since.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: I have that section here, but I was just asking whether, as a matter of fact, shares were actually issued. The provision is that if shares are issued they shall be issued to the Minister of Finance in trust for His Majesty. What I am asking now is whether shares were actually issued, and if so, how many.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
Shares were issued to
the extent necessary to qualify direotors. I am not quite certain as to the number each director must have, but in the short time I was in the Department of Finance I signed transfers to qualify directors of the Canadian National system. The shares are held-if my memory serves me correctly-,by His Majesty, except the shares necessary to be held by direotors; and the executed transfers in blank so that the matter could be dealt with as occasion necessitated.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: I am distinguishing between the different companies.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: Oh, yes.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
My right hon. friend is
speaking, I think, of shares in the various companies taken over.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
No, the directors are
directors of the Canadian National. If my hon. friend will look at the last annual report of the system he will find how it is made up. They are divided into three blocks; first a block of shares that belonged to the government of this country, the railways belonging to the government; that is the old Intercolonial, the National Transcontinental, the Prince Edward Island railway and so on. Then you have a summary of those mileages, and I think it says "Canadian government railways." Then you have the old Canadian 
Northern and its subsidiaries; and then the Grand Trunk and its subsidiaries, which included the Grand Trunk proper, the Grand Trunk Western and various subsidiaries that comprised what was known as the Grand Trunk system. I dare say it is within the mind of the committee that the Grand Trunk system was made up of a very large number, some fifty-six odd companies. That is the reason, I think, that it used to read "the Grand Trunk system" as distinguished from the Grand Trunk Railway. Then you have the Grand Trunk Western, which was ait one time included in what was called the Grand Trunk system, but for the sake of facility in handling the American as distinguished from the Canadian part of the system it was spoken of separately. It was of course and still is a separate entity, incorporated, if I remember aright, under the laws of the state of Michigan. And there was the Grand Trunk Pacific. Those three together constitute what is 'called the Canadian National system of railways, and under the aot of incorporation the shares representing the corporate entity are held by His Majesty. But the act provided for directors of the Canadian National Railway company as well as of these subsidiaries, the lives of which have still to be maintained-and it is an enormously expensive thing unfortunately. You will find in the annual report the story of all these companies.
Certainly directors of the Canadian National system are qualified from time to time. I cannot at the moment tell the hon. member for Shelburne-Yarmouth what shareholding is necessary-perhaps I can find out from the deputy minister. I am informed that only one share is necessary to qualify a director. Those shares are in the Canadian National system. Of course there have to be qualification shares with respect to the various subsidiary companies. For instance the Grand Trunk Western still has corporate entity; has a president, vice-president and all the machinery to maintain its corporate existence. The Canada Atlantic is still an entity, because there are certain securities outstanding, but the Canadian Grand Trunk owns the Canada Atlantic. The same is true with respect to the Central Vermont, that is another striking illustration. It will be remembered that it was reorganized; is carried in the balance sheet as the Central Vermont Railway, Inc., and the shares of that enterprise are held by the Canadian National system. The securities of course are deposited in the treasury. We guaranteed Canadian Northern bonds to discharge the liabilities created by

C.N.R.-C.P.R. Bill
the rehabilitation and reorganization of the Central Vermont system as it now stands. I do not think there is the slightest doubt- though it can be ascertained, because they are in the vaults-that shares have been issued in the Canadian National system and they are held in the name of His Majesty through the Minister of Finance.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: That is the only point I wanted to have cleared up-whether shares had been issued by the Canadian National system as distinct from the subsidiary companies which are still extant and shares of which are held by His Majesty.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: No, they are held by the company.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: The shares of the Canadian National Railway Company incorporated by chapter 172 of the revised statutes of Canada are not the same shares as those to which my right hon. friend has been referring, which are the shares of .the individual constituent companies. I was asking whether there really were shares issued of the Canadian National Railway Company as such to which subsection 6 of section 9 would apply. I do not think my right hon. friend is correct; perhaps I misapprehended what he said, but I do not think any share qualification is required for the directors of the Canadian National.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: Each man, as appointed, has been qualified.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: I did not know that, but it may be so. The statute expressly provides that there shall be directors, so I do not think there can be a share qualification required. I was going to suggest to my hon. friend the minister that this amendment now under discussion is inseparably intertwined with subsection 6 of section 9, which appears to take away some control by His Majesty, exercised by the governor in council or otherwise, and it is really that section which gives rise to the great apprehension on this side. I should like to ask if there would be any real objection to doing away with this subsection. I know we are jumping ahead, but I think this is the time to consider that point. If you did away with that subsection, which does not seem to be in the Canadian National Railways Act, that apprehension would be removed, and then we would be back to section 23 of the Canadian National Railways Act.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
I suggest, with all due
respect, that we should leave subsection 6 of section 9, because it is quite a long distance
ahead. When we come to that we will consider the various aspects of that subsection and if necessary, as the Prime Minister has said, we can come back to this section. Let us deal with this section now, and then when we come to subsection 6 of section 9 we can deal with those questions.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
The sponsor of the
amendment is not here, but could we not have the amendment stand until we come to subsection.6? That was suggested by the right hon. leader of the opposition and I think assented to by the Prime Minister.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: Perhaps the hon. gentleman would withdraw his amendment with the consent of the committee; then if he wishes to submit it at some other point he can do so.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
Why can we not let the
section stand and go on?

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: The only objection I have is that we started on section 1, the short title, and after spending all afternoon on it we let it stand. Now we have spent one whole evening and a part of an afternoon on this section, and we are asked to let it stand. I should like to make a little progress. The Prime Minister has agreed to come back to this section if, in future discussions, anything comes up making that course of action advisable. Surely that should be satisfactory to my hon. friend. There is no trick to it; we are not trying to get this section passed by anything like that, but I do not wish to have all the sections stand as we go along. We would have to start all over again.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
I do not think that is
so; I believe a general discussion is necessary in the beginning and expedites the matter in the end.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
If the hon. gentleman
looks at Hansard he will find the general discussion which took place on the motion for second reading. I would refer my hon. friend to pages 24 and 25 of the annual report, where he will find a list of the constituent companies making up the whole.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
If the
minister will read subsection 2 of section 2 he will find the words "parts II and III," so we can discuss those parts under the very section we are discussing now.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
I do not think that
gives us the power to discuss those parts.
C.N.R.-CP.R. Bill

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: Might I ask the minister if he would consider substituting for paragraph (a) of section 2 a provision similar to that which was inserted in the Maritime Freight Rates Act, merely stating that the provisions of section 179 of the Railway Act shall apply.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: I rise to a point of order, Mr. Chairman. We have a distinct amendment before the committee, and I understand that the hon. member is referring now to an entirely different amendment. I respectfully submit that we cannot discuss a further amendment until we dispose of the amendment now before the committee.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: I think the hon. gentleman is anticipating what the hon. member for East Algoma may say. I should like to hear what the hon. gentleman wishes to say.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: I merely suggest that the minister might take under consideration the insertion of a paragraph which would bring section 179 of the Railway Act into operation.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: Again I rise to a point of order, Mr. Chairman. We are discussing a distinct amendment which deals with the abandonment of branch lines.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: If I understand the matter correctly there is before the committee at the moment an amendment to subsection 1 of section 2 which must be disposed of before another amendment may be considered. If the hon. member for East Algoma wishes to submit another amendment after this has been disposed of he will be quite in order in doing so. Might I ask, for my own information, whether this is a correct citation in the amendment? I cannot find any Canadian National Railway Act of 1920.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: What is the amendment? I thought one had been moved and disposed of.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
My information was that there was before the committee an amendment to subsection 1 of section 2, by adding thereto a clause which will read as follows:
(d) the provisions of section 23 of the Canadian National Railways Act, 1920-

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: That is the title of the Canadian National Railways Act.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: I cannot find that statute.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: It is in the revised statutes of 1927.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: I do not wish particularly to help my hon. friends with their amendment, but I am informed that 1920 should not be there, that it should be called merely the Canadian National Railways Act.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: In the revised statutes of Canada it is cited as the Canadian National Railways Act, 1920. As a matter of fact the hon. member for West Lambton mentioned the fact to me and wondered why it should be so described.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: I am informed that 1920 was the date when it was passed, and that those figures do not form part of the title of the act.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: The title is so given in the revised statutes of Canada.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
I do not
desire to raise any litigious question, but the right hon. leader of the opposition sent me a copy of the bill, in pamphlet form, in which it is indicated that the correct title should be Canadian National Railways Act. A period follows those words, and then we have the figures 1920, which is a reference to the year in which it was passed. According to the statute itself the correct title is the Canadian National Railways Act, with no reference to the year.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: We will not find out for sure until we get the revised statutes.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: Is there any objection to my striking out the figures 1920 in the amendment?

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
I would suggest that the
chairman wait until we get the revised statute, so that we may see how it is described there.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: Subject to correct designation shall the amendment carry ?

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: No.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
I want to point out that
it is rather difficult to dispose of section 2 until we dispose of the proposed amendment in some way or other, or make some arrangement to have it stand until we have considered the other sections. After the long discussion the other evening I thought perhaps we were nearly of one mind with regard to the inadvisability of having any of these lines abandoned or scrapped without an order of the railway board, particularly those lines belonging to the Canadian National Railways,

C.N.R.-CJ>.R. Bill
with which I think the people of this country are more intimately concerned. Do I understand the minister to say that in his opinion, and according to the best advice he can get on the subject, that cannot be done now without an order of the board?

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: Yes, so far as the Canadian National is concerned.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: Then do I understand the minister to mean that in future it should not be done without an order of the board, so there will be no change?

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: There is no change so far as Part I is concerned, which part deals entirely with the Canadian National Railways. That is my best information, and I think it is correct.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
The point about which I
am concerned is that branch lines shall not be abandoned or discontinued without an order of the board. If we are assured of that it meets many of my difficulties. I take it from what the minister says that that is his view- that it cannot be done now under this act.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
I said that under part I
of this bill no change wias being made. When part I becomes law, together with the rest of the bill, the conditions will be in my opinion the same as they are now. So far as parts II and III are concerned, the conditions may be different, but we are dealing with the preliminary portion of part I. Part I deals distinctly with the Canadian National Railways.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: I am not greatly concerned whether it is done by part I, or II or III, or preserved by anything contained in any of these parts, so long as I know that lines cannot be abandoned without an order of the railway board. That is very important to the people of the country, particularly in the rural sections.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
I have no desire to give
to the committee any information that is not correct. I say that so far as parts II and III are concerned, the cooperative measures, it probably does make a difference, and the arbitral board as supreme in that case. As the Prime Minister says, there may never be an arbitral board, because the two railways are now showing a greater disposition towards cooperation than they 'have ever done in the past. If. however, an arbitral board is set up, it will be supreme in this matter, and if it were decided to abandon part of a line either of the Canadian Pacific or of the 53719-251
Canadian National, and to utilize a section of the other railway, by joint agreement, there is no doubt in my mind that the arbitral tribunal would be supreme in that respect.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
If that is so I
object most decidedly to such power being given to any board. We know that Mr. Beatty has suggested that 5,000 miles of railway could be disposed of, and then to give any board that ever existed such authority as is indicated, without the endorsation and consent of the government, is simply scandalous. I object to it with all the vehemence and earnestness at my command, and in the strongest language I am capable of. I know what will be done under this authority; the authority will be exercised and exercised to the limit, and the national railway will be the sufferer.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: What does my hon. friend insinuate-that the purpose of the bill is, in some insidious way, to wreck the Canadian National Railways?

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
I think that the
government should be the protector of the people they are governing; the government should protect the country and its railway property from .any possible depredations and dismantling.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
It is precisely for the
purpose of protecting the country that this legislation is being put .through. It is being enacted with a view to having the two railways in the future operate more economically than up to recently they have been doing; for the Canadian National was in danger of wrecking not only itself but the whole financial structure of the country.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: Does that apply to the Canadian Pacific Railway too?

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: The Canadian Pacific Railway could not wreck the financial structure of this country except of course by reflex action. It is a private corporation for which we are not responsible, and if it went into bankruptcy such injurious effects as might follow would be reflected in the country only indirectly. But the Canadian National Railways could not be allowed to go into bankruptcy.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
We have the Canadian
National Railways because private lines went into bankruptcy.

C.N.R.-C.P.R. Bill

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: I am not going to discuss the history of the railways. No one knows better than my hon. friend what unnecessary expenditures have been made in connection with the Canadian National.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: Voted for by everyone.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: I am not questioning that; I am not discussing the history of these matters, nor am I making any references to the late government. I am simply pointing out the situation as it exists. The hon. member for Melville stood up and implied that there was something in this legislation that had for its purpose not the protection of the people but the wrecking of the Canadian National Railways. I do not remember the exact words he used, but that was their effect. Now I resent that. I do not believe that any government, either this one or the late government, would be so derelict in its duty at this time as to attempt to wreck the Canadian National Railways, and I think it is about time that all hon. members took that attitude. Indeed, I go a step further; I think it is about time that writers on behalf of the Liberal party, such as Mr. Deachman, stopped sending out lies about this government attempting to wreck the national railways, and telling about our driving business from those railways into the hands of the Canadian Pacific-falsehoods sent out under the frank of the Liberal whip. I think it is about time my hon. friends opposite regarded such an attitude as disgraceful to anyone. I have criticized my hon. friends; I criticized them when they were in power and since they have been in opposition I have also been critical of them. But I have never accused them of intentionally trying to wreck the Canadian National Railways. I think they made mistakes, and I do not wish to say more in that regard at the moment; but, I repeat, I have never thought of accusing them of attempting to wreck the system, and I think that any suggestion of that kind on their part now is unworthy of them. No decent Canadian would attempt such a thing, and I resent the implication of my hon. friend from Melville.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: Mr. Chairman-

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: I am not going to imply anything now; I am going to say something definite.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: The hon. member for West Middlesex (Mr. Elliott) has the floor.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
Go on.
[Mr. Power.!

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: I am wound up now; let me run down.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
Do I
understand that the hon. member for West Middlesex gives the hon. gentleman the floor?

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: Go on.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: I was going to say that when we were sitting on the other side of the house, being then in power, and hon. gentlemen opposite were on this side, led by another gentleman now in the Senate, we witnessed on more than one occasion the other chamber throwing out proposed branch line after branch line, holding back the prospective national road for a sufficient length of time to enable the Canadian Pacific to bob in ahead of the Canadian National and cover the very same territory. Was that a friendly act towards the Canadian National Railways? I have in mind particularly the Kelvington line and the Bengough, both in Saskatchewan. The Canadian Pacific got in ahead of the Canadian National, the proposed Canadian National line was slaughtered in another place, although the Canadian Pacific line served largely, and in the case of the former, entirely, the same territory. I could cite a number of branch lines which the other chamber held back long enough to allow the Canadian Pacific Railway to get into some of the best territory in Saskatchewan. Were such acts friendly to the Canadian National. Is it any wonder we suspect the designs and intentions of the government under this bill? It is not the same government, admittedly, nor is it the same leader, but it is the same party-the Conservative party-and their attitude has been the same from the time Sir Henry Thornton took the saddle up to the present. It has never been any different at any time that I know of.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: If the Senate threw out bills of the Canadian National Railways and permitted bills to go through for the Canadian Pacific, enabling the Canadian Pacific to go into Canadian National territory, why did not the hon. gentleman as a member of the government of that day hold up the Canadian Pacific bills?

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: How could you get it past the Senate? The Senate blocked it once and would block it again.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
The hon. gentleman could have stopped the Canadian Pacific bills; it was during his regime that the Canadian Pacific was permitted to go into the territory as he has indicated.

C.N.R.-C.P.R. Bill

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: It was done in the other chamber. We did all we could to get it as far as that chamber but it could get no further, and this occurred not once but half a dozen times. .

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: You could have stopped the Canadian Pacific bills.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: Now that the air is clear once more and everybody is in good humour, may I ask the minister this question. Is it the intention of the government that no branch lines of the Canadian National shall be abandoned except by order of the railway board, as in the past? If that is the case, I think we can make some headway; if it is not the case, I must say that I am very much opposed to making it easier to get rid of branch lines.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
May I point out to my
hon. friend that the Canadian National Railway Company is made up of the Grand Trunk and certain branch lines. As my leader has said, the Canadian National Railways is made up of the Grand Trunk and some of its subsidiaries; it is made up of the Canadian Northern and some of its subsidiaries, and it is made up of the government railways. Up to the present the Canadian Northern and the Grand Trunk Pacific could abandon lines without submission to the Board of Railway Commissioners, whereas the Canadian National Railway Company could not. The Grand Trunk could not abandon lines without submission to the railway commission, but the Canadian Northern and the Grand Trunk Pacific could and can at the present time just the same as the Canadian Pacific. The Canadian Pacific can abandon lines but the Canadian National Railway Company cannot and it is only to that that section 23 applies.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
If hon.
members will pardon me, I should like to know just to what section this amendment applies.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: I regret that I led the chairman astray. I said that the act should be the Canadian National Railways Act, 1920, whereas it should be the Canadian National Railways Act.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
With
the approval of the committee, the amendment will be changed by striking out the figures "1920."

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: Incidentally, the hon. member contradicted the minister.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext: I include the minister in my regrets.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATIONAL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
It does seem to me that
my question could be answered. Is the minister satisfied that the legislation which he is sponsoring makes it clear that branch lines or portions of the Canadian National Railways cannot be abandoned without an order being first obtained from the tribunal?

speechtext: I must point out that we are getting into parts II and III which deal with the question of arbitral tribunals. maintopic: CANADIAN NATION AL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
If my hon. friend refuses
to change his amendment, then I am sorry we cannot accept it. I have already stated t.o the leader of the opposition the reasons why the tribunal proposed under the present bill is in my opinion superior to such a tribunal as the hon. gentleman suggests. First of all, under the tribunal to be constituted in accordance with this legislation, both railways will be represented, whereas they would not be represented if the Board of Railway Commissioners were the tribunal. They would be represented by witnesses, it is true, but they would not be represented on the court. Secondly, and this is very important,-I have discussed it with those who, in a judicial capacity, should know more about the matter than most of us-a tribunal constituted in such a manner as this will be, whereby the members, after hearing the case and arguing it among themselves, can sit down at a round table conference and go into it thoroughly, as an ordinary court or the Board of Railway Commissioners could not do, would be in a far better position to come to a reasonable decision than would be the railway board in the same circumstances. These are the chief arguments and I think they should commend themselves to the committee. On these grounds I must decline to accept the hon. gentleman's amendment.

maintopic: CANADIAN NATION AL-CAN ADI AN PACIFIC RAILWAY BILL
speechtext:
I submit that the
reason given by the minister for preferring a tribunal such as is proposed in part III of the bill is not a good reason at all. If that is a sound argument, then it seems to me that in courts of law counsel for the respective litigants should sit with the judge instead of with their -clients. I took the trouble to read the evidence given before the committee in the other house and I find that even the leader of that house was more or less in sympathy with the idea of having the Board of Railway Commissioners; but he advanced the same reasons against that course as the minister has stated to-day. The Board of Railway Commissioners is a body that has been functioning in 'Canada for some twenty-nine years and it has the confidence of the people. The head of that board is the man whom the government regards as the outstanding arbitrator in connection with disputes between the two railways. That being so, surely a body that has been trained in settling disputes in railway matters is more competent to dispose of such disputes as will arise now than any other body that might be set up. What shall we have under the arbitral -tribunal referred to in part III? A dis-

pute will arise between the two railway companies and -the tribunal will come into operation. The best men of both companies will be appointed and their representatives will sit with the chairman of the railway board in order to decide the dispute. But these men appointed by the two railways will not foe in a position to be arbitrators at all; they will be simply counsel for the respective railway companies and 'they will be sitting at the table to advance the arguments of their own particular companies. The result is that in all oases the chairman of the railway board will foe left to decide the dispute. There would not be a dispute if the two representatives sitting with the chairman could possibly agree, because they would agree before the chairman sat in with them, if there was any possibility of an understanding. We want to have a board that will be able to give a decision after listening to the arguments advanced. When we come to part III, if this section is amended as proposed, other changes will have to be made. Under the Railway Act at present one commissioner may form a quorum in certain cases and in other cases two. It will be necessary to change part III of the bill, or to make a change somewhere else, to indicate how the tribunal 'Shall be comprised. In my opinion the tribunal should consist of ait least three members of the railway board. I am afraid I cannot withdraw the amendment, because I think that the tribunal set up under this legislation should be the best trained body we have in this country, and that is the Board of Railway Commissioners.

speechtext: I wonder wha-t position my hon. friend would take with regard to the board of arbitration set up under the disputes investigation act, such as is now set up where disputes arise between any of the railway companies and the employees. Would he suggest that the dispute be referred to the Board of Railway Commissioners, and that that board would be the proper tribunal to consider the matter?
